- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes or positive sentiment; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >80), model tends to overshoot and continue upward; apply a downward correction of 3–8% in the first 5–7 days following such events.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.33 or below), model often fails to fully reflect downward pressure; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% for each negative sentiment unit.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.5), model tends to overreact; cap forecast increase at +3% above recent 18-day average to avoid overcorrection.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in downward corrections; if true outcome drops below 70, model often takes 2–4 days to adjust; apply a 1–2% daily downward correction until price stabilizes.
